title: Align TodoWrite tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all TodoWrite improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go TodoWrite matches the basic tool name, required todo item fields, accepted status enum, empty-list clearing, all-completed persisted clearing, session/agent scoped todo keys, and the base model-facing success text. It is not exact parity with the TS baseline. The main remaining gaps are task-v2 mutual exposure gating, strict top-level schema validation, Go-only validation/output additions, permission bypass behavior, verification-nudge gates and formatting, structured result semantics, TodoWrite v1 state/resume/reminder lifecycle, remote-agent todo progress extraction, and focused parity tests for these edges.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Go exposes TodoWrite together with task-v2 tools instead of enforcing TS mutual gating
improvement_points.description: TS keeps TodoWrite and the task-v2 tools mutually exclusive: TodoWrite disables itself whenever isTodoV2Enabled() is true, while TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate/TaskList are only added when task-v2 is enabled. Go has equivalent RuntimeScope enablement logic but SetupRegistry registers TodoWrite and all task-v2 tools unconditionally. Deferred tool visibility can hide TodoWrite initially when ToolSearch is present, but ToolSearch can still load it and direct registry execution can still call it.

improvement_points.title: Go does not enforce TS top-level strict-object validation or required todos
improvement_points.description: TS validates TodoWrite input with z.strictObject({ todos: TodoListSchema() }), so missing todos and unrecognized top-level keys fail before call execution. Go publishes todos as required, but parseInputOrError uses json.Unmarshal into TodoWriteInput; unknown keys are ignored and omitted todos becomes a nil slice that Execute treats as an empty successful write. Go's JSONSchema type also does not express additionalProperties:false.

improvement_points.title: Go rejects several inputs that the TS TodoListSchema accepts
improvement_points.description: TS TodoItemSchema requires content and activeForm to have length at least 1 and status to be one of three values; it does not trim whitespace, reject duplicate content, or cap list length. Go trims content/activeForm for emptiness, rejects duplicate trimmed content, and rejects lists over MaxTodoListSize=200. These checks may be useful robustness policy, but they are not exact TS parity.

improvement_points.title: Go can route TodoWrite through the generic permission handler while TS always allows it
improvement_points.description: TS TodoWrite explicitly declares no permission checks and returns allow. Go's loop calls PermissionHandler for every tool unless a pre-tool hook returns permissionBehavior allow; TodoWrite has no special bypass. In ask-always or rule-based modes, unknown/non-low-risk tools can prompt or deny when no prompt is available.

improvement_points.title: Verification nudge gate and text formatting do not match TS
improvement_points.description: TS emits the verification nudge only when VERIFICATION_AGENT is enabled, the tengu_hive_evidence growthbook flag is true, the call is on the main thread, all todos are completed, there are at least three todos, and none contains /verif/i. Go emits the nudge based only on the todo list content and allDone state, has no TodoWrite main-thread/subagent check, does not call the existing isVerificationAgentEnabled helper, and formats the nudge with a raw Go string containing literal backslash-n sequences instead of actual blank lines.

improvement_points.title: Go structured result does not exactly mirror TS output data
improvement_points.description: TS returns a structured data object with oldTodos, newTodos, and verificationNudgeNeeded; importantly, data.newTodos is the input todos, even when the persisted AppState is cleared because every todo is completed. Go serializes TodoWriteResult into Metadata["todoWriteResult"] rather than returning a typed data object, and it fills NewTodos from the persisted post-clear list. ToolResultBlock.Metadata is not JSON-marshaled to transcript/API blocks, so external JSON event consumers may not see the structured result at all.

improvement_points.title: Go adds a regression warning to TodoWrite output that TS does not emit
improvement_points.description: TS TodoWrite model-facing content is only the base success message plus the optional verification nudge. Go additionally detects completed-to-noncompleted regressions and appends a model-facing warning, plus regressed metadata. That changes the tool result content for replay scenarios and can affect model behavior.

improvement_points.title: TodoWrite v1 state and resume lifecycle are file-backed in Go but AppState/transcript-backed in TS
improvement_points.description: TS TodoWrite v1 stores todo lists in AppState.todos under context.agentId or session ID, and SDK/non-interactive resume hydrates that AppState from the last TodoWrite tool_use in the transcript. Go TodoWrite writes to .claude/todos/<scope>.json through TodoStore and Load only reads that file; the session repository loads transcript messages but there is no TodoWrite transcript extraction/seeding path visible in the Go code. This is a behavioral state difference, not merely storage formatting.

improvement_points.title: Go does not implement TS TodoWrite stale-use reminder attachments
improvement_points.description: TS periodically injects a todo_reminder attachment when TodoWrite is available, no brief tool suppresses it, enough assistant turns have elapsed since the last TodoWrite and reminder, and the current AppState todo list should be surfaced. Go's query loop injects skill and MCP instruction deltas before query preparation, and its post-compact attachment provider restores several runtime surfaces, but there is no equivalent TodoWrite turn-count reminder or todo_reminder attachment in the searched Go paths.

improvement_points.title: Go remote/agent result surfaces do not extract TodoWrite progress like TS RemoteAgentTask
improvement_points.description: TS RemoteAgentTask scans append-only SDK logs for the latest TodoWrite tool_use and stores a todoList on the remote task state whenever the log grows. Go agent summaries and AgentCompleted results track latestToolUse and transcriptPath, but searched Go agent result structs do not include todoList or a TodoWrite-log extraction path.

implementation_subtasks.title: Gate TodoWrite and task-v2 tools with RuntimeScope.IsTodoV2Enabled
acceptance_criteria: Interactive/default sessions register task-v2 tools and do not register TodoWrite.
Non-interactive sessions without CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS register TodoWrite and do not register task-v2 tools.
CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS truthy forces task-v2 tools and disables TodoWrite.
Disabled tools are absent from registry lookups and cannot be loaded through ToolSearch.
Prompt task-management guidance reflects the actually registered task system.

implementation_subtasks.title: Make TodoWrite input validation match the TS Zod schema
acceptance_criteria: Missing top-level todos is rejected before state mutation.
Unknown top-level keys are rejected for TodoWrite, matching z.strictObject.
The published schema can represent additionalProperties:false if Go schemas are serialized from types.JSONSchema.
Duplicate content, whitespace-only non-empty strings, and lists over 200 items follow TS behavior unless a separately documented non-parity policy is explicitly enabled.
Existing valid empty-list clearing still succeeds.

implementation_subtasks.title: Bypass generic permission prompts for TodoWrite while preserving hook blocking
acceptance_criteria: A deny PermissionHandler is not invoked for TodoWrite, matching TS checkPermissions allow.
PreToolUse hooks can still deny/block TodoWrite.
PreToolUse hooks with updatedInput still feed the updated input into TodoWrite.
Other tools continue to use the generic permission handler unchanged.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align TodoWrite verification-nudge gating and formatting
dependencies: TW-TASK-001 if the implementation needs reliable main-thread vs subagent scope from RuntimeScope
acceptance_criteria: Default Go TodoWrite does not emit a verification nudge unless the TS-equivalent verification feature and hive evidence gates are enabled.
Subagent-scoped TodoWrite calls do not emit the nudge.
Main-thread all-completed 3+ item lists without verification content emit the nudge only when gates are enabled.
The nudge starts with actual blank lines before NOTE, not literal backslash-n text.
TodoWriteResult.VerificationNudgeNeeded follows the same gate as the model-facing content.

implementation_subtasks.title: Make TodoWrite structured result data match TS outputSchema
acceptance_criteria: TodoWrite structured result has oldTodos, newTodos, and verificationNudgeNeeded matching TS names and semantics.
For an all-completed write, persisted state is cleared but structured newTodos remains the input completed list.
Structured output is available to the same class of internal/SDK observers as comparable Go tool structured data; if metadata remains the carrier, tests prove it is parseable and event-visible.
Model-facing tool_result content remains base plus optional nudge only.

implementation_subtasks.title: Remove or non-default-gate Go-only TodoWrite regression warnings
acceptance_criteria: A completed-to-pending rewrite returns the same model-facing content TS would return: base success plus any TS-valid verification nudge only.
No regressed metadata is emitted by default for TodoWrite.
If the project keeps regression detection as an intentional Go enhancement, it is behind an explicit opt-in flag and default parity tests assert it is off.

implementation_subtasks.title: Restore TodoWrite v1 state from transcript on resume
acceptance_criteria: When TodoWrite is the active task system and no valid todo file exists, resume scans transcript messages for the last TodoWrite tool_use and restores its todos.
Invalid TodoWrite transcript inputs restore an empty list, matching TS safeParse fallback.
Task-v2 sessions do not hydrate TodoWrite state from transcript.
A corrupt or missing .claude/todos file does not silently erase a recoverable transcript todo list.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement TS-style TodoWrite stale-use reminder attachments
acceptance_criteria: Todo reminder turn counts ignore thinking messages and count assistant turns like TS.
Reminder injection is skipped when TodoWrite is not an available tool.
Reminder injection is skipped when the brief/SendUserMessage-equivalent workflow suppression applies, if that surface exists in Go.
Injected reminder carries current todos and itemCount, and repeated reminders obey the TS turn spacing.
Task-v2 task reminders remain separate and are not conflated with TodoWrite reminders.

implementation_subtasks.title: Extract TodoWrite progress into Go remote/agent task state
acceptance_criteria: Go can scan agent transcript/log messages for the latest TodoWrite tool_use and parse todos with the TodoWrite schema.
Completed/remote agent state exposes todoList in the TS-equivalent surface without changing existing latestToolUse behavior.
Invalid TodoWrite inputs in logs produce an empty todoList, matching TS safeParse fallback.
The scan is append-only/log-growth aware or otherwise avoids repeated full rescans in polling paths.
TodoWrite input validation and schema behavior match the original TS implementation for all report gaps.
TodoWrite model-visible output and structured result data match TS golden fixtures.
TodoWrite runtime side effects, state transitions, permission decisions, and error branches listed in improvement_points are implemented or explicitly documented as intentionally out of scope.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
